course_summary:
ISEN 632 / AERO 636 | Human Factors Engineering for Aerospace Designs | Spring 2026
Instructor: Nancy Currie-Gregg | currie-gregg@tamu.edu
Meets: N/A | Online
Grading: Lecture activities [10%], Quizzes (4) [35%], Homework [25%], Project (Interim deliverables 45%, final deliverables 55%) [30%] — A: 89.5-100%, B: 79.5-89.4%, C: 69.5-79.4%, D: 59.5-69.4%, F: ≤ 59.4%
Topics: Extravehicular activity (EVA)-unique design considerations, Extravehicular activity (EVA), Spaceflight-associated neurovestibular effects, Neurovestibular effects, spatial disorientation, Visual effects and illusions, Vestibular effects and illusions, Microgravity effects on health and performance, Sustained accelerations, vibrations, Dynamic accelerations, crew injuries, High altitude, radiation, Anthropometric considerations for spacecraft, Anthropometric considerations for aircraft, Anthropometry, Safe haven design (anthropometry & habitability), Habitability considerations for long-duration space missions, Aerospace vehicle interface design – displays, Aerospace vehicle interface design: controls, Aerospace vehicle designs, Human reliability measures, human error mitigation strategies, human error management, Human-Systems Engr requirements, human-system integration requirements, human-system integration challenges, human-system interface design, human-system design optimization, human-system design improvement, aerospace human-system design process, human-systems design principles, Aerospace HSI design/mitigation needs, Concept of operation, proposed mitigations, countermeasures, published literature critique, proposed design solutions assessment, system characteristics, human performance assessment results, survey methods for human workload, physical workload evaluation, cognitive workload evaluation, physiological measures, subjective measures, Human performance evaluations, usability evaluations, human cognitive performance, human physical performance, human performance in aviation systems, human performance in space systems, human sensory attributes, motor attributes, cognitive attributes, Aerospace health and human performance risks, health and human performance, Physiological issues, psychophysiological issues, principle physiological concerns, psychophysiological concerns, Physical stressors, Cognitive stressors, safety considerations, Safety considerations for human-systems, fatigue, attention, situational awareness, mission performance, aviation environments, spaceflight environments, aerospace environments, aerospace applications, aerospace design project
Tools: MS Teams, Zoom, Canvas, Knovel, EBSCO
Prerequisites: Graduate classification or approval of instructor
